name: Wipro Limited
moat_justification: Scale and sticky multi-year enterprise relationships are real, and ROIC proxy has stayed above the cost of capital (~13% FY23-25, gross margin stable ~29-31%) — but the labor-arbitrage model is replicable, pricing power is weak, AI automation deflates the legacy ADM/infra base, and returns have converged from ~20% (FY16/FY21) toward ~13% while USD revenue has been flat for four years and peers (TCS, Infosys, Accenture) take share.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 19 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 24.1%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency INR converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Wipro Limited Form 20-F for FY2026 (filed 2026-06-02), cover page, securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) of the Act: American Depositary Shares, each represented by one Equity Share (also stated in Part I, Item 7)) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.5%) vs bull-case tier C (12.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable cash generator with a weak, eroding moat (4/10): USD revenue flat for four years, ROIC proxy down to ~13%, and even the bull case reaches only 12.2% IRR at $1.94 — it clears the 15% hurdle only below $1.21 (weighted IV@15%).
moat_for: Top-tier Indian IT scale: ~$10.4B revenue, 236,328 employees (Q2 FY27 release), multi-year outsourcing relationships with genuine switching friction
ROIC proxy still above cost of capital — 12.8-13.1% FY23-25 — with gross margin stable at 28.7-30.7% over the last five fiscal years
Durable cash conversion: operating cash flow ran well above net income in recent prints (Q2 FY27 OCF 165.8% of net income per the results release), funding dividends and repeated buybacks
moat_against: Labor-arbitrage delivery model is replicable — no proprietary product, data or network effect; TCS, Infosys, Accenture and HCLTech bid the same wallet
AI automation deflates traditional application/infrastructure work and clients demand the productivity be passed through — pricing power is weak
Growth has lagged peers for a decade: USD revenue flat FY22-25, IT services +0.6% YoY constant currency in Q2 FY27, large-deal bookings down ~59% QoQ in that release
ROIC proxy down from ~20% (FY16 and FY21) to ~13% (FY23-25) — returns converging toward the cost of capital
Client global capability centers (insourcing) compete for the same spend
